 College Football Playoff rankings predictions: What 2026's second CFP top 25, bracket could look like
 How the College Football Playoff format will work in 2026-27 
 Share 
 After seven ranked vs. ranked games, the next College Football Playoff rankings are bound to change. Before the rankings are unveiled by the CFP committee, I predict where each potential top 25 team could land.
 The second of six CFP top 25 reveals happens on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Ahead of the announcement, here's a prediction of how the committee could rank its top 25 teams. Note that these are my predictions and mine alone. I take a look at head-to-head results, schedule strength, games against ranked teams, and more to help rank the teams as I think the CFP committee will do so. You can read the CFP committee's official protocols here.
 College Football Playoff rankings predictions: The first top 25 projections | Week 11
 These predictions are as of Sunday, Nov. 8.  
 Georgia (8-1) | LW: 2 — Georgia is the likely No. 1 team after adding a top-10 win over Ole Miss. The CFP committee had the Bulldogs over Utah last week, likely due to a 47 rank difference in strength of schedule (SOS). Even with a loss on the resume, I think UGA gets the top spot this week.
 Utah (9-0) | LW: 3 — Utah picked up a win in the Holy War over BYU. That joins Houston and Arizona as ranked wins for Utah, but the SOS only ranks 69. While the undefeated Utes have a great argument for No. 1, I think the committee only ranks them at No. 2.
 Alabama (7-2) | LW: 5  — The committee surprised many with Alabama at No. 5 last week. Then the Tide went out and dominated LSU on the road. That win adds to Alabama’s resume that includes the No. 1 strength of schedule in the country. With Alabama already in the top “pod” of teams, I think the committee uses last week’s performance to move the Tide up.
 Texas (7-2) |  LW: 7 — The CFP committee uses pods of six in their rankings, and Texas likely joins the top pod of teams after adding another ranked win over Missouri. The Longhorns moved to 4-0 against ranked opponents, and have a win over a common opponent in Ohio State when compared to last week’s No. 4 Indiana. Those factors will move Texas into position to have a first-round bye.
 Notre Dame (8-1) | LW: 11 — I think the CFP looks at Notre Dame’s win over Miami (Fla.) where it led by as many as 21 points in the second half and launches the Fighting Irish into the top five. Notre Dame’s win has it as a one-loss team with the 33rd-best SOS and a win over the then-No. 1 team in the country. Notre Dame only ranked No. 11 last week because of a lack of a signature win, but with said win on the resume, it has exactly what the committee was looking for.
 Miami (8-1) | LW: 1  — Miami will drop out of the top five this week after being a “unanimous” No. 1 in the committee room a week ago. The loss to Notre Dame drops it down a pod, but the No. 25 SOS will keep the Hurricanes ranked highly in the CFP committee’s eyes.
 Tennessee (7-2) | LW: 13  — Tennessee added a win over Kentucky to a win over Alabama. The most recent top-10 win won’t be enough to get the Volunteers into the top pod discussion, thereby keeping Tennessee’s head-to-head win over Alabama out of the discussion. However, the wins will allow Tennessee to climb into the second pod of teams and into the top 10.
 UCLA (9-0) | LW: 8  — UCLA will be the top-ranked Big Ten team this week. The reason the undefeated Bruins only ranked No. 8 last week was because “their schedule wasn’t as strong as other comparable teams.” While Oregon’s win over Ohio State helps UCLA in the SOS department, it’s still not enough to move the Bruins.
 Indiana (8-1) | LW: 4  — Indiana’s SOS took a major hit this week as Howard, Western Kentucky, Northwestern, Rutgers, Nebraska, Ohio State, Michigan and Minnesota all lost. That’s every team Indiana has played except North Texas. That resume was why Indiana ranked No. 4 last week, but it’ll now be why the Hoosiers fall after a bye week.
 Kentucky (7-2) | LW: 6  — Even after a blowout loss to Tennessee, I think Kentucky stays in the top 10 thanks to metrics. The Wildcats have a top-five SOS in the country, plus two ranked wins over LSU and South Carolina. The committee won’t knock UK too far after losing to a fellow top-10 team.
 BYU (7-2) | LW: 9  — BYU will drop out of the top 10 after a loss in the Holy War. The Cougars only lost by eight points, and they do have a win over Notre Dame. That adds to a top-30 SOS that can keep BYU in the playoff bracket for now.
 Texas Tech (8-1) | LW: 15  — Texas Tech joins the top 12 after beating West Virginia in a shootout. A loss to a Cincinnati team that two fellow ranked Big 12 teams beat in the weeks following keeps the Red Raiders from the projected bracket.
 Wake Forest (8-1) | LW: 16  — The committee highlighted how Wake Forest was playing in recent weeks and the Demon Deacons followed that up with a shutout win over an FCS school. That’s one way to impress and rise up the rankings.
 Ole Miss (7-3) | LW: 10  — Ole Miss suffered its second blowout loss of the season, this time at home to Georgia. However, ranked wins over LSU and Missouri keep the Rebels on the playoff bubble as the committee’s highest-ranked three loss team.
 Houston (7-2) | LW: 17  — Houston bounced back from a loss to Utah with a win over Cincinnati. The Cougars still won’t have a win over a currently ranked team, but with just two losses the committee will move them up.
 Oregon (6-3) | LW: 23  — The pod system might keep Oregon from rising to No. 16 in the rankings, but I think Oregon’s win over Ohio State might launch them up a few pods. If Oregon is in the same pod as both USC and Ohio State, the committee will have to rank the Ducks above both teams, even with three losses.
 Southern California (7-2) | LW: 20  — USC moves up to No. 17 after a bye thanks to losses around the country.
 Ohio State (6-3) | LW: 12  — Here’s where the CFP will lean on head-to-head. Ohio State will have to rank behind Oregon and USC after losing head-to-head, and in front of Iowa after winning head-to-head. Add in Ohio State’s win over Indiana and you have a Buckeye team in the middle of this week’s rankings.
 Iowa (7-2) | LW: 19  — Iowa handily beat Northwestern and only has two losses. However, the Hawkeyes don’t have any wins over currently ranked teams which keeps them put in the rankings.
 South Carolina (5-3) | LW: 21  — South Carolina enters the top 20 after defeating Texas A&M. The Gamecocks have won four straight games, including a win over Tennessee.
 Boise State (8-1) | LW: 25  — Boise State has won eight straight games and will be on the edge of the top 20. The CFP committee likes how the Broncos played against Oregon when the Ducks were at full strength, so it’ll be a quality loss on the resume.
 Arizona (7-2) | LW: 22  — Arizona won a nailbiter over TCU. The Horned Frogs are a sub-.500 team, so that close win will make it hard for the committee to move the Wildcats up.
 LSU (6-3) | LW: 14  — LSU drops out of the top 20 but stays ranked after losing to Alabama. The CFP committee values how LSU has dominated in wins, but without any currently ranked wins, the Tigers have work to do.
 Missouri (6-3) | LW: 18  — Missouri won’t drop out of the rankings after losing to Texas. However, the Tigers don’t have any wiggle room after Florida drops from the rankings.
 Duke (7-2) | LW: NR  — I think Duke has a shot at joining the rankings this week. The Blue Devils have the solid strength of record and a nonconference win over an Illinois team that’s likely also in contention for a spot in the rankings.
 What the bracket could look like
 First Teams Out: No. 12 Texas Tech, No. 13 Wake Forest, No. 14 Ole Miss, No. 15 Houston
 Notable College Football Playoff rankings questions
 What teams are in what pods this week?
 The Alabama-Tennessee discussion last week brought a renewed focus on the pods the CFP committee uses. That will only be increased giving the circular nature of wins that we’ll see.
 How will the committee rate Notre Dame which beat Miami, but lost to BYU. What about the same BYU team that added a loss to Utah this week?
 The same goes for all of the SEC teams and even the Big Ten teams that are likely to be in the bottom half of the rankings like Oregon, USC, Ohio State and Iowa.
 This week will provide more clarity on how the committee views all of the ranked results.
 What new team joins the rankings?
 We don’t know what other teams are on the committee’s radar after just one set of rankings. Yet, the No. 24 team lost last week so we are almost guaranteed at least one new team. Will it be a Group of Six team like New Mexico? Or will it be another Power Four team?
